# ROM-editor coverage summary

Decision document for the paused Product Studio work, from `DRAGONBYTE-Z-ROM-EDITOR-COVERAGE-001`. The census is `docs/research/ROM_EDITOR_SYSTEM_CENSUS.md`, the matrix and counts are `docs/research/ROM_EDITOR_COVERAGE_LEDGER.md`, and the normative machine-readable record is `docs/research/rom_editor_coverage.json`.

## 1. The denominator, and how it was derived

**40 accepted editor-relevant systems.** They were enumerated from evidence first and counted second, and the set was frozen by an independent read-only reviewer with veto power over it before any count was taken. The reviewer's first finding was that the draft's totals did not match its rows; every figure below is now recomputed from the rows by `tests/unit/test_rom_editor_coverage.py`. The denominator is therefore a research result, not a target: it says how many distinct engine systems were found, not how many the product ought to have.

The 15 generic editor facilities (address read, safe write, semantic search, reference lookup, arbitrary byte write, undo, validation, rebuild, patch export, provenance and the rest) are reported separately and are **not** in the denominator: a facility is a product capability, not a game system. The fixed 24/24 capability registry is a third, separate record, is untouched, and is not this denominator.

### Baseline drift measured while this ticket was open

This census measures `486e3c665929a8dc57c63b7915f74606e30ccb0d`, the pinned baseline, and its row set was frozen and reviewed there. While the ticket was open, `origin/master` advanced to `f3955e1b9fc4fba012ceedb7cc9f8a8f8db0f4d0` (the baseline is an ancestor). The merges since the baseline are `cc9265f Merge branch 'ticket/dialogue-token-productization-001' into 'master'`; `f3955e1 Merge branch 'ticket/friend-v3-cold-boot-acceptance-001' into 'master'`. The capability registry is unchanged between the two commits. The product change is 3 files, +443 lines: a new tools/webfoot/token_dictionary.py (430 lines), tools/webfoot/dialogue.py +7, tools/webfoot/compressed_dialogue.py +6, plus docs/research/DIALOGUE_TOKEN_PRODUCTIZATION.md and FRIEND_V3_COLD_BOOT_ACCEPTANCE.md.

Two rows are affected: `dialogue-control-codes`, `dialogue-records`. This census is measured at the pinned baseline 486e3c6, and its row set was frozen and reviewed there. The dialogue token merge landed after that commit and ships a production token encoder, a dictionary codec and an authored-window refusal (tools/webfoot/token_dictionary.py), so row dialogue-control-codes, which records that no token authoring shipped, and row dialogue-records, whose recovered ceiling is quoted for the pre-token fitter, are correct as of 486e3c6 and may be conservative afterwards. Re-measuring those two rows against the merged tree is a separate bounded task and was not done here.

The ticket pins the baseline, the fixed product facts are stated at it, the frozen row set was reviewed against it, and the registry is unchanged between the two commits, so the census keeps its stated measurement commit and declares the drift instead of re-deriving facts against a tip that moved mid-ticket.

## 2. Coverage per game

| state | Buu's Fury | LOGII | LOG1 | family-wide cells |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| FULLY_EDITABLE | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| PARTIALLY_EDITABLE | 19 | 1 | 0 | 20 |
| SEMANTIC_READ_ONLY | 4 | 4 | 1 | 9 |
| KNOWN_BUT_UNSUPPORTED | 8 | 0 | 0 | 8 |
| UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED | 9 | 35 | 39 | 83 |
| N_A | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |

Writable cells: **20 of 120 measured = 16.67 percent**, and that is a cell count, not a system count. The family-wide writable count is over (row, game) cells and several writable cells are one product path: Create Chunk backs map-chunk-containers and part of map-layout-chunk-grids; the placement clone and move contract backs placement-records, area-object-array-tables and behaviour-attachment-authoring; the object palette recolour backs object-palettes and actor-sprite-registry; PNG import backs sprite-frame-records and actor-sprite-registry. Five capabilities carry about ten writable cells, so the percentage must be read with the per-title counts and not as ten independent systems.

**Zero systems are FULLY EDITABLE at the strict definition, and that is the finding rather than an artefact.** Every writable domain carries a boundary that matters to ordinary hacking: 341 of 452 maps for the chunk grid, five of about fourteen map-record fields with no UI, a refused 169-class warp family and no deletion, no new text ids, clone-only placements, one record per dialogue container, one palette entry at a time, one added sprite identity per image, and one trigger contract out of the engine's set. The product is genuinely useful and it is not yet unrestricted anywhere.

Per-game differences, in cells: Buu's Fury has 19 of 40 cells writable and is the only title with a broad writable set; LOGII has one writable cell, its text table, plus four read-only domains including its own script encoding; LOG1 has none and is identity-only. 39 of LOG1's 40 cells and 35 of LOGII's 40 cells are `UNKNOWN_UNMAPPED` on a NOT_INVESTIGATED basis, which is a statement about this lab's evidence, not about those games.

## 3. Engine knowledge is not editor support

Engine knowledge, family-wide cells: **PROVEN** 14, **SUBSTANTIAL** 13, **PARTIAL** 12, **MINIMAL** 11, **UNKNOWN** 70.

The distinction is the point of the census. Several domains are well understood and cannot be written at all (the event resource pool, the item table, fonts, portraits, UI graphics, the executable code). Several are partly understood and writable (map chunks, warps, dialogue, appearances, palettes). Almost none are both fully understood and unrestricted. Audio is neither understood nor writable, and progression, techniques, enemy behaviour logic, the save format and global flags are understood at MINIMAL or worse because no boundary was found for any of them.

## 4. Top findings

1. **Four counted object arrays per area, not one.** The map record's `+0x04` is a pointer to a structure carrying four count bytes and four array pointers (`+0x14`/`+0x18`/`+0x1C` stride 4, `+0x20` stride 8). The SDK models `+0x14` only, so three of four engine-owned object families are invisible. Recorded as INFERRED and disputed, because a tracked note reads `+0x04` as a count and the dereference contradicts it.
2. **The mobile-object record count is not the coverage number that matters, the array mechanism is.** Three of four families have no reader at all, which is a structural gap rather than a length limit.
3. **The item table is bounded and has no editor.** 83 records of 52 bytes at `0x083BD2F8` with a consumer, a class bit, four text indices, a price and two pools; the product has no item module and no item UI.
4. **The event resource pool is bounded and has no element layout.** 522 pointers, 127,328 bytes, tiling proven, internal element boundaries not recovered.
5. **An entire audio row is unknown**, and the instrument could not search for it: no region, no table, no consumer, no register constant.
6. **The save format is unknown while a 16 MiB expansion ships**, so nothing certifies that a generated image round-trips a retail save.
7. **Five tracked research claims were refuted by the bytes**, including a string table that is a numeric curve and an ARM region that is Thumb.
8. **Four original compilation units are named by the cartridge itself**, which is the best naming oracle in the image and is used by no ticket.
9. **The capability registry's own proof field is stale for `sprite-new`**: it reads `application` while its evidence cites a runtime parity run. A bookkeeping defect, reported not fixed.
10. **Nothing in the product can write an arbitrary byte**, and the write stack refuses any change without a named semantic owner. That is a correctness property, and it is also why integrated hex editing needs new core authority rather than a new window.

## 5. Largest editor gaps, ranked

1. **Integrated hex editing with safe arbitrary byte authoring that preserves the attributable-change invariant.** - A prior owner decision already makes integrated hex a 1.0 requirement; the core currently has no anonymous byte-write entry point at all, so this is core authority before it is a surface.
2. **A byte-range-to-semantic-owner index that answers for the whole image, and a search that can scan raw bytes as well as classified structures.** - Without it, a hex editor writes bytes the product cannot attribute, and the raw browser cannot answer what owns a range.
3. **A container encoder that can grow a filtered or packed payload.** - It gates every insertion capability: new graphics, new dialogue text, new sprite payloads. Named in the roadmap as the Phase 3/4 gate.
4. **Stat-table and map-header surfaces over the SDK models that already exist.** - The SDK reads and writes these domains today and the product neither names nor surfaces them, so the claim to be a general-purpose editor is materially overstated without them. This is surfacing plus registry honesty, not new research.

Then, in order: the three unmodelled object families, the save format, audio, the script handlers' meaning, and the graphics and font families.

## 6. Where a hacker still leaves DragonByte Z

1. **Ghidra plus an assembler or patcher** - Any change to what the executable does: damage formulas, enemy behaviour, a bug fix, a new feature. Nothing in tools/webfoot assembles, compiles or emits an instruction.
2. **custom Python script over an unidentified format** - Audio: no region, table or consumer identified and no product module exists.
3. **standalone tile or graphics editor plus a custom decoder** - UI/HUD, fonts and glyphs, portraits, title and static screens, and map graphics below the chunk level: enumerable at best, never writable.
4. **mGBA debugger** - IWRAM-resident code, save writes, the sound mixer, and any causal question about which consumer reads a structure at run time.
5. **Ghidra over the script VM** - The game-level meaning of most of the 266 native handlers, which blocks general script authoring and all LOGII dialogue.
6. **custom Python script over the compressed stream** - No production encoder exists, so any change whose encoded size changes must be hand-built.

The largest exit is code: nothing in the toolkit assembles, compiles or emits an instruction, so any change to what the executable does is a Ghidra plus patcher job. The second largest is the missing container encoder, which gates adding anything whose encoded size changes.

## 7. Cross-game

Buu and LOGII share compilation-unit names, the bytecode interpreter directory and the EEPROM family; they diverge in drive letter, assertion encoding and save-library variant. LOG1 shares none of it measurably: zero declared tables, zero preserved developer strings, and the Buu actor-sprite table is refuted at the same offset in both siblings. No Buu structure is projected onto LOGII or LOG1 in this census; where a title was not investigated, the cell says so.

## 8. Raw bytes and hex

Already in core and needing only a surface: address read and jump, project-backed safe writes, canonical-base comparison, modified-range and changed-byte tracking, semantic ownership of ranges, reference lookup, semantic search, validation, rebuild, patch export and provenance. Needing real core authority: **arbitrary byte write** (the write stack is owner-first and an anonymous byte edit breaks the attributable-change invariant unless it is admitted through the same validation) and an owner index over the whole image, where known ownership is deliberately incomplete and an unowned range is UNKNOWN, not free. Undo exists only per editor in the UI; core has no undo for a hex surface to use.

## 9. V1.0 recommendations

**V1.0 ESSENTIAL**
- Integrated hex editing with safe arbitrary byte authoring that preserves the attributable-change invariant.
- A byte-range-to-semantic-owner index that answers for the whole image, and a search that can scan raw bytes as well as classified structures.
- A container encoder that can grow a filtered or packed payload.
- Stat-table and map-header surfaces over the SDK models that already exist.

**V1.0 NICE_TO_HAVE**
- Patch export and modified-range visualisation in the desktop shell.

**POST-1.0**
- Portrait, UI/HUD and font authoring.
- Map graphics below the chunk level, and tileset authoring.

**RESEARCH FIRST**
- The three unmodelled per-area object arrays and their record families.
- The save format and whether expansion preserves it.
- Audio: locate the engine, the tables and the sequence or sample data.
- The game-level meaning of the 266 script native handlers.

**NOT_PRODUCT_WORTHY**
- A dedicated editor for the compiler-embedded assertion strings, the colour lookup block and the debug debris.

These are recommendations. The integrated hex editor remains V1.0 ESSENTIAL by prior owner decision, and no owner decision is invented here.

## 10. Highest-value reverse-engineering targets

1. **Decode the element types of the three unmodelled per-area object arrays** - Turns three of four engine-owned object families from invisible into classifiable, which is the largest single map-system coverage gain available.
2. **Recover the container encoder's initial literal width** - Unblocks every insertion capability in the product.
3. **Recover the event resource pool's element lengths** - 127,328 bytes with a proven 522-entry index and no recoverable element boundary: nothing in that span is authorable until lengths exist.
4. **Name the stat fields through their consumers** - Turns two readable tables into meaningful editors and closes the 20-byte-stride family that no consumer is known for.
5. **Identify the save serializer** - Closes a correctness risk in the shipped expansion path and enables save work.
6. **Find the audio engine** - An entire unknown row; a sound-register watch in the debugger is the cheapest route.

## 11. Product Design impact

1. **Do Maps / Entities / Scripts & Text / Graphics / Data survive the census?** The five provisional categories still describe the data, with one correction: Graphics is really two domains at different maturity (payload graphics and sprites, which are partially editable, versus UI, HUD, fonts, portraits and static screens, which are not), and Data is the load-bearing category rather than a leftover.
2. **Is another first-class category required?** One: a raw and semantic browser over byte ranges with an integrated hex surface, owning address navigation, range-to-owner and owner-to-range lookup, modified-range tracking and arbitrary byte authoring. It is the only category that can reach the 54 percent of the image that no domain row owns.
3. **Which cross-navigation edges are safe to design?** map to layout to chunk to map graphics; map to warp to destination map; object array to placement to behaviour to script to text; script root to owning record (item or map); sprite identity to animation to frame to container; appearance to sprite id to text; item to text indices and to its script.
4. **Which are still unproven?** placement to the sprite it draws; enemy stat record to its character sprite; map trigger to the script it fires; shop to the item list it sells; any relationship into the audio system.
5. **What must the Data and raw browser own?** address and range lookup for the whole image; range to semantic owner and owner to range; the owned-coverage population and its honest gaps; raw byte search alongside semantic search; modified-range and dirty-byte state; canonical-base comparison for a range.
6. **What must the hex editor bridge?** an anonymous byte-write owner admitted through the existing validation, or the attributable-change invariant breaks; range-to-semantic overlay for the whole image, not just declared tables; undo and redo, which core does not own today.
7. **Is Product Design ready to resume Stage 3?** Yes for the census's own categories and the two Essential core authorities named above; no for scoping a dedicated editor for audio, UI/HUD, fonts, portraits, static screens or map graphics below the chunk level, each of which is RESEARCH FIRST.

## 12. What is not claimed

No runtime observation was added by this ticket; the runtime lane launched no emulator. No compiler identity, save format, audio format, event element layout or LOG1 structure beyond identity is established. The ROM surface classification is a lower evidence rung than the bytes and four of its region classes were refuted. And no percentage here replaces or adjusts the fixed 24/24 capability registry.
